prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: EN · Issue tracker (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 13px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "ID" · longest unbreakable word 34px · one-line width 66px
  col 2: header "Title" · longest unbreakable word 81px · one-line width 349px
  col 3: header "Severity" · longest unbreakable word 52px · one-line width 52px
  col 4: header "Assignee" · longest unbreakable word 58px · one-line width 58px
  col 5: header "Status" · longest unbreakable word 54px · one-line width 68px
  col 6: header "Updated" · longest unbreakable word 55px · one-line width 77px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 651px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 650px.
Fixed: content, font, 13px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Your understanding so far: {"purpose":"Triage and track engineering bugs: identify each issue, judge severity and status, and see who owns it and when it changed.","reading":"Readers use ID + Title as the row anchor, compare Severity and Status for triage, then check Assignee and Updated for ownership and recency; row-level scanning matters more than deep reading of any one column.","groups":["ID + Title: issue identity and scan anchor","Severity + Status: triage state","Assignee + Updated: ownership and recency"],"keep_intact":["ID values such as BUG-2041","Severity labels such as Critical","Assignee handles such as m.garcia","Status single words such as Backlog, and ideally phrases such as In progress","Updated dates/values"],"may_wrap":["Title at word boundaries","Status phrases at spaces if width is tight","Long titles may take two lines; short metadata should not be split"]}

The first image is the one-line content overview. The other images are real browser renders of your current designs:
Design r0A: widths [87, 224, 73, 79, 89, 98] · table 651×314px · row heights [33, 53, 33, 53, 53, 33, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0B: widths [87, 238, 73, 79, 75, 98] · table 651×314px · row heights [33, 53, 33, 53, 53, 33, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 2 lines · mid-word splits 0
Design r0C: widths [87, 200, 79, 90, 96, 98] · table 651×334px · row heights [33, 53, 33, 73, 53, 33, 53] · column headers wrapped 0/6 · tallest cell 3 lines · mid-word splits 0

Look carefully at each render as a whole and in detail. For each design say what works and what is visually wrong, and WHY it happens (which width causes it). Then propose up to 3 improved designs: refine the most promising, fix the problems you saw, and try a new idea if an important alternative is unexplored. If no design can be meaningfully improved, set "done": true and return no new designs.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"critique":[{"design":"name","good":"","problems":"","cause":""}],"done":false,"designs":[{"name":"short-name","widths":[int px],"change":"what you changed and why"}]}
